policy_title: Increase overseas aid and climate finance
stated: Restore international aid to 0.7% of GNI, raising it to 1% by 2033. Increase the climate finance budget to 1.5% of GNI by 2033, with an additional contribution to a newly established Loss and Damage Fund. Make finance and technology available to support low-income countries in climate action.

source.quote: Greens would ensure that the UK’s existing climate finance commitments are delivered in full and are genuinely new and additional to aid spending. Elected Greens would push for the UK to: • Go beyond restoring international aid to 0.7% of GNI, raising this to 1% by 2033. • Increase the climate finance budget to 1.5% of GNI by 2033, with an additional contribution to a newly established Loss and Damage Fund in order to help climate vulnerable countries to respond to increasingly severe storms, floods and rising temperatures. • Make finance and technology available to support the development of environmentally and socially sustainable economies of low-income countries to tackle the causes and impacts of the climate and nature emergencies.

bearing_set.reason: The policy explicitly directs large-scale public finance (1.5% of GNI) and technology transfer toward reducing emissions in low-income countries and funds Loss and Damage — directly targeting global emissions trajectories, which affect the UK's own climate exposure through the global commons.

Committing to aid at 1% of GNI plus climate finance at 1.5% of GNI (potentially ~2.5% of GNI combined, up from ~0.5% current ODA) represents a very large unfunded spending increase; without a specified funding mechanism, this moves the debt path or requires substantial tax rises — a non-negligible hit to O12's sustainability indicator.

membership_note: The policy's primary effects are global (climate and development) and fiscal (very large spending commitment). Domestic fundamentals (O1–O5, O7–O11, O13–O15) are not directly moved: any second-order prosperity or security effects via global stability are too diffuse and indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
